facts.fact_text: Ilinden is an association based in south-west Bulgaria, in an area known as the Pirin region or the geographic region of Pirin Macedonia.
During the period 1990-97 Ilinden each year tried to organise meetings at sites in Pirin Macedonia to commemorate certain historical events.

On 25 March 1998 the second applicant and three other members of Ilinden informed the mayor of Sandanski that Ilinden intended to organise a meeting on 19 April 1998 at the Rozhen monastery to commemorate the anniversary of the death of Yane Sandanski, a historical figure buried there.
On 18 April 1998 a number of members and followers of Ilinden from towns and villages in Pirin Macedonia tried to approach the Rozhen monastery by cars and by buses.
On 10 July 1998 Ilinden notified the mayor of Petrich that it planned to hold a meeting in the area of Samuilova krepost on 2 August 1998.

On 2 August 1998 a number of members and followers of Ilinden travelled by car to Samuilova krepost, but all roads leading to the site were blocked by the police who were stopping the cars and turning them back.

On 7 September 1998 Ilinden notified the mayor of Blagoevgrad that it planned to lay wreaths on 12 September 1998 at the memorial of Gotze Delchev, situated in the centre of Blagoevgrad, to observe the seventy-fourth anniversary of the alleged killing of certain Macedonian activists by agents of the Bulgarian government.
On 7 April 1999 Ilinden notified the mayor of Sandanski that it planned a commemoration at Rozhen monastery on 25 April 1999.
On 25 April 1999 members and followers of Ilinden tried to approach the Rozhen monastery by cars.
On 27 April 1999 Ilinden notified the mayor of Blagoevgrad that it planned to lay wreaths at the memorial of Gotze Delchev on 4 May 1999.
On 12 July 1999 Ilinden notified the mayor of Petrich that it planned to hold a meeting at Samuilova krepost on 1 August 1999.
On 11 April 2000 Ilinden notified the mayor of Sandanski that it intended to organise a commemorative meeting on 22 April 2000 at Rozhen monastery.
On 10 July 2000 Ilinden notified the mayor of Petrich of its intention to hold a commemorative meeting on 30 July 2000 at Samuilova krepost.
On 1 September 2000 Ilinden informed the mayor of Blagoevgrad that it wanted to hold a commemoration at the memorial of Gotze Delchev on 12 September 2000.
On 4 April 2001 Ilinden notified the mayor of Sandanski that it would organise a meeting on 22 April 2001 at Rozhen monastery.
On 27 April 2001 Ilinden notified the mayor of Blagoevgrad that it intended to lay flowers at the memorial of Gotze Delchev on 4 May 2001.
On 12 July 2001 Ilinden notified the mayor of Petrich of its intention to hold a meeting on 29 July 2001 at Samuilova krepost.
On 23 August 2002 Ilinden notified the mayor of Blagoevgrad that it wanted to hold a commemoration at the memorial of Gotze Delchev in the centre of Blagoevgrad on 12 September 2002.

On an unspecified date in July 2003 Ilinden notified the mayor of Petrich that it planned to hold a meeting at Samuilova krepost on 2 August 2003, to commemorate the one-hundred anniversary of the Ilinden uprising.
On 28 August 2003 Ilinden notified the mayor of Blagoevgrad that on 12 September 2003 it intended to organise a commemoration at the memorial of Gotze Delchev in Blagoevgrad.

On 3 April 1998 the mayor of Sandanski informed the second applicant and the other members of Ilinden that he prohibited the meeting planned for 19 April 1998 at the Rozhen monastery, as the municipality was preparing a commemoration.

On 3 April 1998 the mayor of Sandanski informed the second applicant and the other members of Ilinden that he prohibited the meeting planned for 19 April 1998 at the Rozhen monastery because another association, which according to the Government was hostile towards Ilinden, had already notified the mayor of its intention to hold a meeting at the same time and place.

On 14 April 1998 the mayor of Sandanski replied that he could not assent to the meeting being held on 18 April 1998, as in the meantime the other association had informed him that their commemoration would last from 18 until 22 April.
On 17 April 1998 the Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office issued a decree ordering the police to take measures to prevent Ilinden from holding a meeting.

On 17 April 1998 the second applicant and several other members of Ilinden were issued written warnings informing them that the planned meeting had been banned by the Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office.
On 18 April 1998 all members and followers of Ilinden trying to approach the Rozhen monastery were turned back by the police who were placed at checkpoints on the roads leading to the monastery.
On 18 April 1998 the passengers of one bus travelling to the Rozhen monastery were forced off and the driver was fined for allegedly driving a vehicle in a state of disrepair.

On 18 April 1998 one person coming by car to the Rozhen monastery was apparently taken into custody by the Sandanski police for ten hours for allegedly failing to produce an identification document, and was ill-treated.

On 15 July 1998 the mayor of Petrich replied that he could not allow the holding of a meeting at Samuilova krepost on 2 August 1998, as another meeting had been planned for the same date and place by a municipal child centre.

On 28 July 1998 the Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office issued a decree under Article 185 § 1 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, ordering the police to take measures to prevent Ilinden from holding a meeting.

The Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office decree of 28 July 1998 reasoned that Ilinden was not registered and hence had no right to organisational or political activities, and that the holding of a meeting would therefore constitute an offence under Article 174a of the Criminal Code.

The Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office decree of 28 July 1998 reasoned that Ilinden was advocating changes in the constitutional order in Bulgaria and that the holding of a meeting would therefore also constitute an offence under Chapter 1 of the Criminal Code.

On 2 August 1998 a number of members and followers of Ilinden travelled by car to Samuilova krepost, but all roads leading to the site were blocked by the police who were stopping the cars and turning them back.

On 2 August 1998 several police officers approached members of Ilinden at the bus station in Petrich, informed them that the meeting had been banned by the Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office, and warned them not to try to reach Samuilova krepost.

The secretary of the municipality of Blagoevgrad informed the head of the local chapter of Ilinden that Ilinden would not receive a written answer and that the municipality would advise the police so that it could prevent the event planned for 12 September 1998.

On 11 September 1998 the Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office issued a decree under Article 185 § 1 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, ordering the police to take measures to prevent Ilinden from holding a meeting.

In the evening of 11 September 1998 the police visited the house of the head of the local chapter of Ilinden in Blagoevgrad and warned him that if he tried to organise the event planned for 12 September 1998 he would be criminally prosecuted.
On 12 September 1998 members and followers of Ilinden tried to approach the memorial of Gotze Delchev in Blagoevgrad, but the police blocked their way.

On 12 September 1998 the police informed members and followers of Ilinden that the Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office had banned the event and read them the decree, but refused to give them a copy.

On 29 April 1999 the Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office issued a decree under Article 185 § 1 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, ordering the police to take measures to prevent Ilinden from holding a meeting.
The Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office decree of 29 April 1999 reasoned that the holding of a meeting by Ilinden would constitute offences under Article 174a and Chapter 1 of the Criminal Code.

On 4 May 1999 members and followers of Ilinden who tried to approach the memorial of Gotze Delchev in Blagoevgrad were stopped by the police, who informed them that the Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office had issued a decree prohibiting the event.
On 4 May 1999 the police read out the Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office decree prohibiting the event to members and followers of Ilinden, but refused to give them a copy.

On 20 July 1999 the mayor of Petrich replied that he could not allow the holding of a meeting at Samuilova krepost on 1 August 1999, as another meeting had been planned for the same date and place by another organisation.

On 27 July 1999 the Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office issued a decree under Article 185 § 1 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, ordering the police to take measures to prevent Ilinden from holding a meeting.

The Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office decree of 27 July 1999 considered that the holding of a meeting by Ilinden would constitute offences under Article 174a and Chapter 1 of the Criminal Code.
On 1 August 1999 members and followers of Ilinden tried to approach Samuilova krepost by cars, but were stopped by police stationed at the roads leading to the site.
On 18 April 2000 the mayor of Sandanski made an order prohibiting the meeting planned for 22 April 2000 at Rozhen monastery, apparently on the ground it would endanger public order.

On 22 April 2000 members and followers of Ilinden tried to approach the Rozhen monastery by cars and were stopped at police checkpoints, where some of the drivers were fined, allegedly for traffic violations.
On 22 April 2000 the police seized material intended for the decoration of a stage which members of Ilinden planned to set up at the Rozhen monastery site.
On 22 April 2000 a vehicle transporting musicians and their instruments to the Rozhen monastery was not allowed to continue by the police.
On 22 April 2000 the cars of members and followers of Ilinden were stopped again at a second police post near the Rozhen monastery and some written materials were impounded.

By a letter of 18 July 2000 the mayor of Petrich replied that he could not allow the event planned for 30 July 2000 at Samuilova krepost, as another association had already applied for authorisation to organise a meeting on the same date.
The mayor of Blagoevgrad did not reply to Ilinden's notification of 1 September 2000.

On 8 September 2000 the Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office issued a decree under Article 185 § 1 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, ordering the police to take measures to prevent Ilinden from holding a meeting.
The Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office decree of 8 September 2000 reasoned that the holding of a meeting by Ilinden would constitute an offence under Chapter 1 of the Criminal Code.
On 12 September 2000 members and followers of Ilinden tried to approach the memorial of Gotze Delchev in Blagoevgrad, but were stopped by the police.
On 12 September 2000 a police officer read out the decree prohibiting the commemoration to members and followers of Ilinden, but refused to furnish a copy of it.

By a letter of 20 July 2001, which was allegedly delivered at the home of a member of Ilinden on 28 July 2001 – a Saturday – the mayor of Petrich prohibited the meeting planned for 29 July 2001 because another meeting had been planned for the same date by a municipal child centre.

On 25 July 2001 the Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office issued a decree under Article 185 § 1 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, ordering the police to take measures to prevent Ilinden from holding a meeting.
On 29 July 2001 a group of approximately two hundred and fifty people tried to approach Samuilova krepost by buses and cars, but were turned back by the police two kilometres before the site.
The applicants allege that on 29 July 2001 the police told members and followers of Ilinden that military exercises were to take place and that they could not continue to Samuilova krepost.
According to the Government, on 29 July 2001 members and followers of Ilinden were informed of the Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office decree prohibiting the event at Samuilova krepost.

On 29 July 2001, after being stopped from reaching Samuilova krepost, the members and followers of Ilinden decided to lay flowers at the memorial of a poet in Petrich, but several dozen police officers blocked their way.
The mayor of Blagoevgrad did not reply to Ilinden's notification of 23 August 2002.

On 12 September 2002 the memorial of Gotze Delchev in Blagoevgrad was surrounded by a group of about twenty persons who were shouting insults, preventing members and followers of Ilinden from initially approaching it.

On 12 September 2002 several persons from the hostile group attacked individual members and followers of Ilinden, broke the flagstaff one of them was carrying, tried to take another flag, tore a poster and took the ribbon from a wreath carried by one of the members of Ilinden.
On 12 September 2002 a member of Ilinden was filming with a camera when one person from the hostile group attacked him from behind and tore the electrical cables of the camera.

On 12 September 2002 the police were present at the memorial of Gotze Delchev in Blagoevgrad and had formed a cordon between the members and followers of Ilinden and the hostile group, but apparently failed to prevent the above incidents.

In a letter of 1 September 2003, which was posted on 5 September and arrived on 9 September, the mayor of Blagoevgrad informed Ilinden that in principle every citizen of Bulgaria had the right to commemorate national heroes such as Gotze Delchev.

In the letter of 1 September 2003 the mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that the remarks contained in Ilinden's notification were unconstitutional and provocative, and were indicative of actions which would infringe the rights of others and would lead to conflicts, as had already happened in the past.
In the letter of 1 September 2003 the mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that in order to organise events, Ilinden had to be registered.

In the letter of 1 September 2003 the mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that there was no need for the planned event to take place in front of the memorial of Gotze Delchev and that its timing was inopportune because another event had been planned for the same time and date.
On 11 September 2003 the police summoned two members of Ilinden and cautioned them in writing to refrain from organising the event planned for 12 September 2003.

On 12 September 2003 the mayor of Blagoevgrad informed Ilinden that he prohibited the planned event, because it would create conditions for the disruption of the public order and would endanger the rights of others.

On 12 September 2003 several police officers approached the members and followers of Ilinden in the centre of Blagoevgrad and read out a decree of the Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office prohibiting the commemoration.

On 24 April 1998 the Sandanski District Court informed Ilinden of its refusal to examine the applications for judicial review on the merits, as they had been submitted on behalf of an unregistered organisation and were vague.
In a judgment of 20 July 1998 the Petrich District Court dismissed Ilinden's application for judicial review.
In its judgment of 20 July 1998 the Petrich District Court held that Ilinden was not duly registered in accordance with the laws of Bulgaria.

In its judgment of 20 July 1998 the Petrich District Court held that as a result of Ilinden's lack of registration, it was unclear who would be the organiser of the event and who would be responsible for order during the meeting, in accordance with sections 9 and 10 of the Meetings and Marches Act of 1990.
In its judgment of 20 July 1998 the Petrich District Court concluded that the lack of clarity as to the organisers of a public event endangered public order and the rights and freedoms of others.
In a judgment of 26 July 1999 the Petrich District Court dismissed Ilinden's application for judicial review.
In its judgment of 26 July 1999 the Petrich District Court held that Ilinden was non-existent as it was not registered.

In its judgment of 26 July 1999 the Petrich District Court held that as a result of Ilinden's lack of registration, it could not be considered as the organiser of, and be responsible for order during the meeting, as required by sections 9 and 10 of the Meetings and Marches Act of 1990.
In its judgment of 26 July 1999 the Petrich District Court held that the lack of clarity as to the organisers of the event endangered public order.
In its judgment of 26 July 1999 the Petrich District Court held that another meeting had been scheduled for the same date and place as Ilinden's planned meeting.
In a judgment of 24 July 2000 the Petrich District Court dismissed Ilinden's application for judicial review.

In its judgment of 24 July 2000 the Petrich District Court found that Ilinden had not been registered and apparently had links with a political party, UMO Ilinden – PIRIN, which had been declared unconstitutional by the Bulgarian Constitutional Court on 29 February 2000 for acting against the territorial integrity of the country (see The United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden – PIRIN and Others v. Bulgaria, no. 59489/00, §§ 21-27, 20 October 2005).
In its judgment of 24 July 2000 the Petrich District Court found that the holding of a meeting by Ilinden could therefore pose a threat to the territorial integrity of Bulgaria.

In its judgment of 24 July 2000 the Petrich District Court found that another, duly registered, association intended to organise a meeting on the same date as Ilinden's planned meeting, and that the parallel holding of two events could endanger public order.
In a decision of 16 September 2003 the Blagoevgrad District Court declared Ilinden's application for judicial review inadmissible.

The Blagoevgrad District Court found that Ilinden's application for judicial review had been filed with the court on 10 September 2003 and had been brought to the attention of a judge-rapporteur at 4.37 p.m. on 11 September 2003.
The Blagoevgrad District Court noted that by section 12(6) of the Meetings and Marches Act of 1990, the time-limit for ruling on the application was five days.

The Blagoevgrad District Court held in its decision of 16 September 2003 that as of that date the issue whether to allow the event planned for 12 September 2003 had become moot and there was no need for the court to rule on it.

According to the Government, on 29 July 2001 members and followers of Ilinden were informed of the Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office decree prohibiting the event at Samuilova krepost.

On 29 July 2001, after being stopped from reaching Samuilova krepost, the members and followers of Ilinden decided to lay flowers at the memorial of a poet in Petrich, but several dozen police officers blocked their way.

On 12 September 2002 the memorial of Gotze Delchev in Blagoevgrad was surrounded by a group of about twenty persons who were shouting insults, preventing members and followers of Ilinden from initially approaching it.

On 12 September 2002 several persons from the hostile group attacked individual members and followers of Ilinden, broke the flagstaff one of them was carrying, tried to take another flag, tore a poster and took the ribbon from a wreath carried by one of the members of Ilinden.
On 12 September 2002 a member of Ilinden was filming with a camera when one person from the hostile group attacked him from behind and tore the electrical cables of the camera.

On 12 September 2002 the police were present at the memorial of Gotze Delchev in Blagoevgrad and had formed a cordon between the members and followers of Ilinden and the hostile group, but apparently failed to prevent the above incidents.

In a letter of 1 September 2003, which was posted on 5 September and arrived on 9 September, the mayor of Blagoevgrad informed Ilinden that in principle every citizen of Bulgaria had the right to commemorate national heroes such as Gotze Delchev.

In the letter of 1 September 2003 the mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that the remarks contained in Ilinden's notification were unconstitutional and provocative, and were indicative of actions which would infringe the rights of others and would lead to conflicts, as had already happened in the past.
In the letter of 1 September 2003 the mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that in order to organise events, Ilinden had to be registered.

In the letter of 1 September 2003 the mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that there was no need for the planned event to take place in front of the memorial of Gotze Delchev and that its timing was inopportune because another event had been planned for the same time and date.
On 11 September 2003 the police summoned two members of Ilinden and cautioned them in writing to refrain from organising the event planned for 12 September 2003.

On 12 September 2003 the mayor of Blagoevgrad informed Ilinden that he prohibited the planned event, because it would create conditions for the disruption of the public order and would endanger the rights of others.

On 12 September 2003 several police officers approached the members and followers of Ilinden in the centre of Blagoevgrad and read out a decree of the Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office prohibiting the commemoration.

On 24 April 1998 the Sandanski District Court informed Ilinden of its refusal to examine the applications for judicial review on the merits, as they had been submitted on behalf of an unregistered organisation and were vague.
In a judgment of 20 July 1998 the Petrich District Court dismissed Ilinden's application for judicial review.
In its judgment of 20 July 1998 the Petrich District Court held that Ilinden was not duly registered in accordance with the laws of Bulgaria.

In its judgment of 20 July 1998 the Petrich District Court held that as a result of Ilinden's lack of registration, it was unclear who would be the organiser of the event and who would be responsible for order during the meeting, in accordance with sections 9 and 10 of the Meetings and Marches Act of 1990.
In its judgment of 20 July 1998 the Petrich District Court concluded that the lack of clarity as to the organisers of a public event endangered public order and the rights and freedoms of others.
In a judgment of 26 July 1999 the Petrich District Court dismissed Ilinden's application for judicial review.
In its judgment of 26 July 1999 the Petrich District Court held that Ilinden was non-existent as it was not registered.

In its judgment of 26 July 1999 the Petrich District Court held that as a result of Ilinden's lack of registration, it could not be considered as the organiser of, and be responsible for order during the meeting, as required by sections 9 and 10 of the Meetings and Marches Act of 1990.
In its judgment of 26 July 1999 the Petrich District Court held that the lack of clarity as to the organisers of the event endangered public order.
In its judgment of 26 July 1999 the Petrich District Court held that another meeting had been scheduled for the same date and place as Ilinden's planned meeting.
In a judgment of 24 July 2000 the Petrich District Court dismissed Ilinden's application for judicial review.

In its judgment of 24 July 2000 the Petrich District Court found that Ilinden had not been registered and apparently had links with a political party, UMO Ilinden – PIRIN, which had been declared unconstitutional by the Bulgarian Constitutional Court on 29 February 2000 for acting against the territorial integrity of the country (see The United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden – PIRIN and Others v. Bulgaria, no. 59489/00, §§ 21-27, 20 October 2005).
In its judgment of 24 July 2000 the Petrich District Court found that the holding of a meeting by Ilinden could therefore pose a threat to the territorial integrity of Bulgaria.

In its judgment of 24 July 2000 the Petrich District Court found that another, duly registered, association intended to organise a meeting on the same date as Ilinden's planned meeting, and that the parallel holding of two events could endanger public order.
In a decision of 16 September 2003 the Blagoevgrad District Court declared Ilinden's application for judicial review inadmissible.

The Blagoevgrad District Court found that Ilinden's application for judicial review had been filed with the court on 10 September 2003 and had been brought to the attention of a judge-rapporteur at 4.37 p.m. on 11 September 2003.
The Blagoevgrad District Court noted that by section 12(6) of the Meetings and Marches Act of 1990, the time-limit for ruling on the application was five days.

The Blagoevgrad District Court held in its decision of 16 September 2003 that as of that date the issue whether to allow the event planned for 12 September 2003 had become moot and there was no need for the court to rule on it.

On 15 October 2002 Ilinden complained to the Sofia Military Prosecutor's Office about the inactivity of the police officers present during the 12 September 2002 meeting and about their failure to secure the peaceful holding of the event.
The Sofia Military Prosecutor's Office carried out a preliminary verification in response to Ilinden's complaint of 15 October 2002 and on 10 December 2002 refused to open criminal proceedings.

On appeal by Ilinden, the Sofia Military Prosecutor's Office decree of 10 December 2002 refusing to open criminal proceedings was upheld by the Sofia Military Appellate Prosecutor's Office on 20 February 2003.

Ilinden further appealed to the Chief Prosecutor's Office, which upheld the refusal to open criminal proceedings in a decree of 6 October 2003, reasoning that Ilinden's allegations were not supported by the facts established during the preliminary verification.

The Chief Prosecutor's Office decree of 6 October 2003 stated that the police had strictly complied with the relevant legal provisions, that although certain members of Ilinden had acted provocatively, the officers had showed restraint and had performed their duties.
